summaries.summary: Speech-related BCI technologies decode brain signals for communication, neuro-prosthetic help, rehabilitation, entertainment, preventive treatments, personal communication, games, and silent communication.
EEG is promising for BCI but challenging, and prior speech intent work mostly classified discrete vowels, phonemes, and words using handcrafted features and linear classifiers.
Articulatory speech production complicates understanding the discriminative EEG manifold, and few works relate brain signals to articulation with satisfactory EEG-only accuracy.
The proposed mixed neural network uses three supervised steps and one unsupervised step to map multivariate EEG time-series inputs to fixed outputs.
Raw EEG preprocessing follows BIBREF17 but omits Laplacian filtering because high-pass filtering may decrease information content in the selected bandwidth.
The framework reduces high-dimensional multichannel EEG by computing channel cross-covariance matrices, rejecting low-cross-covariance channels, and encoding electrode connectivity.
A four-layered 2D CNN decodes spatial connections and a four-layered LSTM explores temporal features from channel covariance matrices in parallel.
The CNN and LSTM penultimate fully connected layers are concatenated into a single feature vector forming joint spatio-temporal encoding.
An unsupervised DAE with 3 encoding and 3 decoding layers and MSE cost reduces dimensionality and cancels background noise effects.
At the third hierarchy level, an Extreme Gradient Boost classifier receives DAE latent vectors and outputs final predicted speech imagery classes.
Evaluation uses KARA ONE with 14 participants, 11 prompts each, 7 phonemic/syllabic categories, 4 words, and five binary phonological classification problems.
PHASE-ONE splits 1913 signals from 14 individuals into 80% train, 10% development, and 10% test, while PHASE-TWO uses leave-one-subject out cross-validation.

Grid-search on the PHASE-ONE validation set selected architectures, with gradient boosting fixed at maximum depth 10, 5000 estimators, learning rate 0.1, regularization coefficient 0.3, subsample ratio 0.8, and column-sample/iteration 0.4.
PHASE-ONE experiments show the mixed network outperforms individual blocks, while LSTM alone often fails above chance and CNN is biased toward the larger class.
The combined network improves mean accuracy by 14.45% over CNN-LSTM, with maximum above-chance accuracy 75.92% and minimum 49.14%.
tSNE visualization for INLINEFORM0 and V/C classification tasks shows the second feature set is more easily separable, explaining performance.
In PHASE-TWO, the network improves over BIBREF17 by 18.91, 9.95, 67.15, 2.83 and 13.70 %, with standard deviation reduced to 5.41%.
The mixed deep neural network investigates subject-invariant EEG mapping to phonological categories and outperforms BIBREF17 and BIBREF18 by an average margin of 22.51%.
This work was funded by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC) of Canada and Canadian Institutes for Health Research (CIHR).
